title: Profiling Loop & Elicitation
subtitle: Running the six-minute passive sweep and opening protective vaults without direct interrogation.

modules.title: The Six-Minute Profiling Loop & Conversational Diagnostics

mentalModel.name: The Two-Stage Sonar Plot
prose: A submarine commander does not enter unfamiliar waters by flooding the ocean with high-powered active sonar pings. Active pinging announces your presence to every vessel within twenty miles, collapsing the very stealth that makes surveillance possible. Instead, the crew runs a **two-stage sonar plot**. First comes the **passive sweep**: engines hushed, hydrophones open, listening to the ambient signature of propellers, hulls, and currents already moving through the dark. Only once a rough bearing takes shape on the plotting board does the operator send a quiet, low-energy **diagnostic ping** to test distance and structure.

The **Six-Minute Profiling Loop** is that two-stage sonar plot translated into live human conversation. Everything built across Tiers 1 through 3—the stillness of **Operator Baseline** (M01), the low-threat gravity of **Authority Architecture** (M02), the somatic strain gauges of the **BToE** (M03–M04), and the motivational cantilevers and switchyards of **Needs**, **FATE**, and the **Decision Map** (M05–M06)—now converges onto a single tactical plotting board: *Six-Minute X-Ray*'s **Behavioral Compass**. Rather than interrogating a counterpart or scrambling to memorize fifty isolated body-language cues, the operator runs an unhurried passive sweep during the opening minutes of natural dialogue, harvesting visual and linguistic telemetry onto a mental index card small enough to fit on a Post-it note.

The fatal mistake at this altitude is **sensor saturation**. An amateur who tries to track blink rates, shoulder angles, pronoun ratios, sensory predicates, and Decision Map pillars simultaneously burns through working memory in thirty seconds. Their gaze hardens, their timing stalls, and their own cognitive strain leaks across the table as **Observer Distortion** (M01). Mastery of the six-minute loop is never about watching *everything*; it is about disciplined triage—capturing four high-yield bearings passively, verifying them with subtle conversational pings, and updating the plot without ever making the other person feel studied.

mechanics.title: Compiling the Behavioral Compass: Phased Triage and the Four-Variable Ceiling
prose: Under live conversational pressure, raw observation fails unless it is compressed into an effortless shorthand. *Six-Minute X-Ray* solves this bottleneck with the **Behavioral Compass**—a circular plotting grid organizing a counterpart's active profile around the perimeter (`DEC` for Decision Map, `HND` for handedness, `SNS` for sensory language, `PRN` for pronoun orientation, `LOC` for Locus of Control, and `NDS` for Primary Social Needs) with a four-cell somatic quadrant and **Gestural Hemispheric Tendency (GHT)** arrows inside the ring.

What makes the compass workable in real time is not superhuman speed, but **phased automation**. *Six-Minute X-Ray* breaks acquisition into four sequential layers: **Visual** (tracking physical telemetry), **Audio** (harvesting linguistic patterns), **Response** (adapting your own phrasing to match the profile), and **Mental** (running the entire compass without paper). Crucially, during live interaction, the visual channel obeys a hard cognitive ceiling: track **no more than four somatic variables at once**—for example, blink-rate shifts (`Br`), finger relaxation versus curling (**Digital Extension** vs. flexion, `Df`), lip compression (`Lp`), and **Dominant Shoulder Retreat** (`Ds`), which flags sharp internal disagreement the moment the counterpart's dominant shoulder pulls backward.

Only when you circle the exact conversational topic that triggered a shift does a raw squiggle become actionable bearing. Notice the quiet elegance of that discipline: you are not cataloging a human being's essence; you are mapping *which specific topics* loosen their fingers into digital extension and which ones pull their dominant shoulder back half an inch.

mechanics.title: Hearing Between the Lines: Linguistic Harvesting (Pronouns, Adjectives, and Sensory Predicates)
prose: While visual telemetry maps involuntary load, spoken language maps how the counterpart constructs reality—a process *Six-Minute X-Ray* calls **Linguistic Harvesting** ("hearing between the lines"). Across three clean audio channels, ordinary small talk leaks structural architecture within minutes:

- **Pronoun Orientation (`Self`, `Team`, `Others`):** Listen to where the speaker places the center of agency. A `Self`-oriented speaker narrates outcomes through *"I," "me,"* and *"my"*; a `Team`-oriented speaker defaults to *"we," "us,"* and *"our"*; an `Others`-oriented speaker anchors around *"they," "people,"* or *"everyone"*. Mirroring their dominant pronoun frame before pitching a proposal removes an invisible grammatical friction that most negotiators never realize they are creating.

- **Positive and Negative Adjective Harvesting:** People carry a tiny, recurring vocabulary of emotional shorthand—the exact adjectives they reach for when something excites them (*"brilliant," "solid," "clean"*) or repels them (*"outdated," "messy," "overbearing"*). Logging three positive and three negative adjectives gives you the counterpart's native valuation dial; feeding their own approval words back into a summary makes an unfamiliar option feel strangely self-authored.

- **Sensory Predicate Channels (`Visual`, `Auditory`, `Kinesthetic`, and `Audio-Digital`):** In *Six-Minute X-Ray*'s review of conversational interviews, speakers reliably drop sensory predicates within roughly the first three minutes (*"I just don't see why"* vs. *"something didn't sound right"* vs. *"there's something that doesn't feel right"*), alongside *The Ellipsis Manual*'s fourth **Audio-Digital** analytical register (*"criteria," "process," "bottom line"*).

Here, epistemic discipline prevents a classic trap. Popular NLP folklore treats VAK predicates as rigid, hard-wired "learning styles" or neurological personality types—a claim that fails controlled empirical testing. Treat sensory predicates strictly as **live lexical alignment**: echoing a counterpart's active metaphorical register (*"let's map out a clear picture"* for a visual speaker, or *"let's test whether this feels solid"* for a kinesthetic one) lowers cognitive translation cost and signals attunement without pretending you have x-rayed their cortical wiring. Over-doing it—stuffing every sentence with theatrical visual jargon—trips the counterpart's mimicry radar and triggers **Psychological Reactance** (M10).

mechanics.title: Directional Telemetry: Gestural Hemispheric Tendency (GHT) and Eye Home
prose: The subtlest bearing inside the Behavioral Compass is directional kinematics: **Gestural Hemispheric Tendency (GHT)** and **Eye Home**. Across both *Six-Minute X-Ray* and *The Ellipsis Manual*, observation starts by discarding the pop-TV myth that looking up-left universally equals truth and up-right equals a lie—a rigid formula that empirical testing dismantled long ago.

What remains observable is idiosyncratic, personal habit. During the first minute of unguarded talk, many subjects consistently favor one spatial side of their body—hands, head tilts, or gaze—when describing pleasant, endorsed topics, and the opposite side when referencing friction or dislike (`ght-lp` for left-positive, `ght-rp` for right-positive). Similarly, **Eye Home** marks the consistent clock-face direction a specific individual glances toward whenever they retrieve routine memories.

The counterintuitive trade-off is knowing how *lightly* to weight this signal. Even *The Ellipsis Manual* explicitly cautions that GHT **must never be relied upon to make outcome-affecting decisions**. Treat GHT and Eye Home strictly as *low-weight secondary corroboration*—a subtle tie-breaker that only matters when it converges with **BToE Stress Clusters** (M03), **Primary Social Needs** (M05), and **Linguistic Harvesting**.

This brings the two-stage sonar plot full circle. Once your passive sweep populates the Behavioral Compass, you transition smoothly into **Module 08's active pings**—replacing blunt, defensive questions with conversational statements that confirm or falsify your hypotheses in real time. The third-order payoff of disciplined profiling is effortless precision: instead of arguing harder against invisible resistance, you speak in the counterpart's native pronouns, adjectives, and decision frame, letting the room open from the inside out.

mentalModel.name: The Pressure-Sensitive Vault Door
prose: Push hard against a heavy, pressure-sensitive vault door and the hydraulic deadbolts slam deeper into the steel frame. The harder you lean your shoulder into the handle, the tighter the seal locks. You do not open a vault like that by applying more outward force; you open it by **equalizing the pressure differential** across the threshold until the bolts retract on their own and the door swings inward under its own weight.

Direct questioning is outward force. The instant a conversation shifts into pointed, rapid-fire questions (*"What is your actual margin on this?"* or *"Who really pushed back on the merger?"*), the counterpart's nervous system registers an interrogation frame. Their **Protective Mask**—first mapped under Laws 2 and 3 (M01)—locks down automatically. Once that steel door seals, you stop receiving raw intelligence and start receiving defensive smoke: **Exclusions** (*"to the best of my knowledge," "as far as I recall"*), **Résumé Statements** listing credentials instead of answering, **Question Reversals** (*"What were you doing Monday?"*), or **Mini-Confessions** tossed out like decoy flares to make you stop digging.

**Conversational Elicitation** is the discipline of equalizing the pressure differential so information flows out voluntarily. Built directly on top of Module 07's passive sonar sweep, it replaces interrogative questions with low-threat **statements** calibrated to human social reflexes—our urge to correct an error, to educate a genuinely curious listener, to reciprocate a candid disclosure, or to soften a compliment. Because the counterpart experiences themselves as *choosing* to offer the detail rather than being cornered into surrendering it, the vault door stays unlatched, **Psychological Reactance** (M10) stays dormant, and they walk away remembering the exchange as an unusually good conversation.

mechanics.title: Equalizing the Threshold: Protective Masks, Deliberate Social Errors, and the Hourglass Method
prose: Before deploying a single **Elicitation Probe**, an operator must lower the ambient threat level of the room. High-polish perfection often triggers suspicion rather than trust; when a counterpart already shows high-barrier defensiveness, pressing harder only accelerates **Observer Distortion** (M01). *The Ellipsis Manual* notes that seasoned operators deliberately bleed off that tension through **Deliberate Social Errors**—small, non-threatening imperfections, minor signs of thriftiness, or an unhurried, slightly unpolished demeanor that signals you are neither a predator nor a prosecutor. Trust can also bypass conscious screening altogether through **covert subjective experience**: when a counterpart casually overhears you handling an unrelated ethical moment with quiet integrity—such as checking with a front desk about returning a lost wallet—they form the impression of trustworthiness without their skepticism filter ever firing.

Once the threshold is calm, structural placement protects the intelligence you gather. *Six-Minute X-Ray* formalizes this architecture as the **Hourglass Method**, anchored in two foundational memory effects: the **Primacy Effect** (humans recall the opening of an interaction with high fidelity) and the **Recency Effect** (we recall the closing just as sharply), while the middle blurs into soft focus. By opening wide on safe, adjacent context, narrowing smoothly into the sensitive topic during the middle third of the conversation, and widening back out into warm, unrelated ground before parting, you ensure the counterpart remembers the rapport of the opening and closing rather than feeling retroactively mined. The trade-off is discipline: rushing the sensitive probe into the first ninety seconds—or ending the meeting immediately after getting the number you wanted—leaves a sharp memory scar that alerts the counterpart's **Protective Mask** before your next conversation even begins.

mechanics.title: The Statement Engine: Pulling Information Without Asking a Question
prose: Direct questions put the listener on the witness stand; declarative statements hand them the steering wheel. Across *Six-Minute X-Ray*, elicitation works by gently tapping five high-probability social reflexes—each requiring zero interrogative pressure:

- **Correcting the Record via Citations & Bracketing:** Humans carry an almost automatic reflex to fix factual errors when they know the real number. By attributing an inaccurate figure or range (**Bracketing**) to an outside source (**Citations**)—such as casually mentioning an article claiming grocery staff just got bumped to $21 an hour—the employee instinctively corrects the record (*"What? No—we only make $14.75 unless you're a manager at $19.50"*) without ever feeling pried into.

- **Flattery & Diffidence:** Compliments are not used here for shallow ego-stroking; they work as a gentle excavation tool because social norms compel people to appear humble (**Diffidence**). Praise a project lead for carrying an entire launch solo, and their instinct to deflect credit often unlocks the hidden operational story (*"It wasn't all me—we hit major setbacks and had to bring in outside contractors from another state to make deadline"*).

- **Informational Altruism (Reciprocal Disclosure):** Offering a calibrated, slightly candid vulnerability of your own—such as admitting a minor workflow headache on your team—creates subtle social permission and reciprocity pressure for the counterpart to match your candor with an equivalent reality on their side.

- **Naïveté (The Urge to Educate):** When someone takes quiet pride in a craft or domain, pairing genuine fascination with honest ignorance (*"I've always wondered how that actually works—I can barely follow the basics"*) unlocks deep, unguarded technical walkthroughs.

- **Indirect Criticism, Eliciting Complaints & Disbelief:** Humans defend what they value and fight to be believed—and the only ammunition available in conversation is information. Routing mild criticism through a third party (*"I keep hearing these models don't hold up past year two"*) prompts a car salesperson to defend the brand by volunteering specific recall details and upcoming engineering fixes. Similarly, expressing calm, curious **Disbelief** compels a speaker to open the floodgates to prove their point.

Every lever here carries an **over-use ceiling**. *Six-Minute X-Ray* explicitly warns that repeating flattery or citations more than a couple of times turns natural dialogue awkward and triggers the exact suspicion you are trying to avoid. Effective elicitation weaves one or two statements lightly into genuine listening, then lets silence do the heavy lifting.

mechanics.title: Reading the Valve: Verbal Armor, Micro-Leakage, and Ethical Containment
prose: Elicitation is never a one-way extraction pipe; it is a real-time feedback loop wired back into Tier 2's sensors (M03–M04). The moment a statement lands near a genuinely guarded fault line, the vault door signals resistance before a single accusation is spoken. Listen for sudden shifts in **verbal armor**: a casual speaker abruptly switching into stiff **Non-Contractions** (*"did not"* instead of *"didn't"*), a sudden **Politeness Spike** (*"No sir, absolutely not, sir"*), **Psychological Distancing** euphemisms that soften harsh facts (*"took"* instead of *"stole"*), or an unprompted **Mini-Confession** offered to buy quick forgiveness and steer you away from a larger issue.

Where inexperienced operators trip is mistaking verbal armor for a cue to press harder. In reality, a sudden spike in **Exclusions** or **Hushing** (hand drifting toward the mouth) during an elicitation pass is a telemetry alert telling you *the pressure differential just spiked*. If you tighten your gaze or double down with sharper disbelief, the **Protective Mask** bolts shut, **Observer Distortion** (M01) floods the room, and you destroy the voluntary channel. The disciplined move is counterintuitive: acknowledge the boundary smoothly, widen back out to the safe outer rim of the **Hourglass**, and let **Autonomic Decay Lag** (M01) reset the room.

Over multiple interactions, the second- and third-order effects of Module 08 separate trusted advisors from short-term extractors. Used recklessly—especially weaponizing **Disbelief** or **Indirect Criticism** to trap peers into embarrassing admissions—elicitation leaves counterparts feeling subtly ambushed hours later once the **Recency Effect** wears off, eroding long-term candor (**Trust-Decay Lag**, M12). Used with restraint and genuine curiosity, conversational elicitation clears the fog of polite avoidance, surfaces hidden constraints early, and leaves both sides with cleaner shared reality.
